observed_checkouts.head: b1770f5b0be397bd4ddc2c976ab6548a7a1eeb7f
observed_checkouts.note: Exact clean upstream source checkout; build outputs are ignored under build/.

PR #20 source archive extracted from the immutable commit object with dirty sibling worktree contents excluded; artifact_sha256 digests the built build/main.wasm artifact, not the archive or source tree, so it is not commit- or tree-binding evidence (see the deferred pr20-source-commit-binding item).

diagnostic_only_probes: relative rule_data Include and @pmFromFile fixture input

deferred_inventory.reason: No host deployment fixture describes VM identifiers, config wrappers, or local and checksum-pinned remote artifact loading. Although the source CRS trees are pinned, no host fixture exercises include directives to verify the expanded bundle and rule order.

Exact per-file hashes, CRS version comments, and source commits are recorded in envoy-coraza/tests/contracts/source-provenance.json. The pinned upstream tree has 50 embedded files (CRS 4.14.0); PR #20 has 54 (CRS 4.28.0). File content explicitly declares Apache-2.0 for 28/50 upstream and 30/54 PR #20 files. The remaining 22 and 24 files lack a per-file license declaration in the pinned source; their license and full origin chain remain unverified, so no blanket license is inferred.

The PR #20 extraction has no .git metadata, and no retained archive bytes, archive digest, or export record binds the inspected tree to commit 266b6ed6a471e26e5c6862a46beb974eb1a0fa52. The source_commit field in source-provenance.json is metadata, not independent binding evidence.

The candidate-only rule-data-ip-match-from-file diagnostic probe supplies client_ip for REMOTE_ADDR, but there is no upstream-parity case or broad connection-variable coverage such as REQUEST_FILENAME; REQUEST_URI matching is covered by other rule fixtures.
The current fixture schema has no chunk schedule or incomplete-inspection outcome; this requires the lifecycle driver and stream implementation.
No fixture currently exercises a t: transform against a request value.
No fixture asserts anomaly score accumulation, thresholds, or early blocking from score actions.
No negative rule fixture demonstrates that a nonmatching request was fully inspected and allowed.
No general matched-rule record is required across all request outcomes; selected probes now require ordered IDs/actions, while broader matched-rule coverage remains open.

Configuration-shape fixtures now require configure.accepted/error observations for root scalars, missing authority references, object policy values and container entries in directive arrays. No executable host runner currently captures those outcomes; chain-member disruptive-action compile rejection also remains unverified.
A bounded local Proxy-Wasm audit callback exists, but the host driver has no normalized audit-log observation, so upstream and candidate audit behavior remains uncaptured.
No host driver starts Envoy with invalid plugin configuration and records the startup result.
The fixture covers successful reload only; no host driver records rejection and continued use of the old generation.

backend_response can carry fixed body bytes, but no response-body boundary case captures chunk scheduling, inspection completeness, or the host outcome when a response exceeds its inspection limit. Request-body N-1/N/N+1 cases are covered; response-limit behavior remains deferred.
The fixture schema carries one request per case, so it cannot describe two distinct concurrent HTTP/2 streams or their per-stream results; this needs a multiplexing host driver.
Worker count is Envoy process configuration rather than a request or plugin fixture input; the host runner must start and observe a multi-worker deployment.
A filter-state set_property failure is represented, but a complete hostcall matrix needs per-call fault injection and terminal outcomes that the lightweight fixture runner does not provide.
Bounded memory-pressure and exhaustion behavior needs controlled Envoy limits, concurrent load, and host resource measurements; no fixture scenario models that campaign.
The connector-only rule_data size/file/count bounds have no faithful upstream parity probe or candidate capture assertion yet.

The candidate-only relative-file and @ipMatchFromFile probes record schema-checked observations but prescribe no candidate outcomes; upstream and PR #20 comparisons omit them, so runtime resolution and matching are not automated coverage.
The upstream and PR #20 CRS trees are pinned, but no fixture proves the effect and ordering of CRS exclusion rules.
Fixtures do not define a multi-chunk body schedule; trailer termination is covered, but fragmented delivery and partial inspection are not.
No real Envoy formatter and downstream access-log consumer fixture verifies filter-state visibility.

The Envoy artifact does not enable Coraza's validate-schema feature, as recorded in the connector handoff; no candidate fixture can exercise @validateSchema resolution from rule_data. The separate rule-data-bounds item remains deferred.
The fixture schema has no WebSocket upgrade or tunnel schedule, and no host capture establishes whether upgraded traffic is rejected or inspected.
The fixture schema cannot model CONNECT tunnel bytes or lifecycle, and no host capture establishes whether tunnels are rejected or inspected.
Fixtures describe finite messages; an indefinite stream cannot be buffered to completion, and no host capture establishes an explicit incompatibility response.
The HTTP/2 gRPC trailer probe does not decode protobuf message frames or application fields; doing so requires a schema-aware decoder not represented by this fixture contract.
The pinned deployment matrix has no verified HTTP/3 host/runtime entry or capture, so HTTP/3 behavior is unestablished.
The WASM connector uses bounded in-memory rule_data and exposes no arbitrary filesystem source, but no candidate host fixture captures this incompatibility.
The Envoy artifact disables Coraza's inspect-file feature, so @inspectFile is unavailable; the pinned upstream behavior and candidate rejection have no host capture. See the connector handoff.
The Envoy artifact disables Coraza's rbl feature, so @rbl is unavailable; the pinned upstream behavior and candidate rejection have no host capture. See the connector handoff.
The local Proxy-Wasm audit callback is not a custom remote transport; remote transports remain unimplemented, and no fixture captures an upstream-versus-candidate transport incompatibility.
